title: The Difference Between Nice and Kind - Nautilus
gist: Teaser for an essay on distinguishing niceness from kindness and the long debate over true altruism, opening with Maximilian Kolbe's self-sacrifice at Auschwitz and Hobbes's claim that all action is self-interested.

insights.claim: In 1941 at Auschwitz, Franciscan friar Maximilian Kolbe volunteered to die in place of stranger Franciszek Gajowniczek, who was selected for starvation in retaliation for an escape.
insights.so_what: Illustrative case for the altruism debate; no market angle.
insights.locator: Perhaps you have heard the story
insights.speaker: Kristen French

insights.claim: Thomas Hobbes argued that every human action is ultimately self-interested, so even costly help relieves one's own empathic distress or feeds pride — a view contested by theologians, economists, philosophers and biologists.
insights.so_what: Self-interest assumptions underpin economic models of behavior.
insights.quote: every human action is ultimately driven by pure self-interest
insights.speaker: Kristen French
